solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Only this much into books, excluding royalty

parts.note: so, as in 'so big', points to a quantity

indicators.note: excluding means the royal letters are taken out of the bookish word

parts.note: someone into books is literary, fond of reading
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty

explanation.surface: A grudging comment that a person reads only so much, never touching books about royals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only' looks like a link meaning merely; it is the definition, meaning alone. ER is the usual crossword shorthand for the Queen, hence royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: An only child is a solitary one: both adjectives mean single, alone of its kind.

clue.text: One way and another keeping a model

indicators.note: keeping means the two ways hold the other words between them

parts.note: ST, street, is one kind of way
RD, road, is another kind of way

explanation.surface: Various methods all retaining a particular template.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a benchmark or exemplar, the sense of model as something to copy.

clue.text: Digest litre — gross!

parts.note: L is the symbol for litre
to gross is to earn before deductions

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at downing a litre of something disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like 'disgusting'; it is the verb, to earn.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to take it in and absorb it, as in study.

clue.text: Eighty divisible by two? All the time

parts.note: eighty is four lots of twenty, read here as twenty fours
a number divisible by two is even

explanation.surface: A maths question: is eighty an even number?
explanation.walkthrough: Eighty is four twenties, which the clue reads as 'twenty fours'; even follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week, so constantly.

clue.text: Parrot took off over large city

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in this down entry

parts.note: a bird that took off rose into the air
LA, Los Angeles, is a big city

explanation.surface: A parrot flew up and away over a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosellas are colourful Australian parrots.

clue.text: Cloud is back in under a minute

indicators.note: back means the combined pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: sub is the Latin prefix for under
min is the usual short form of minute

explanation.surface: A weather report: a cloud returns in less than sixty seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB and MIN, written backwards, give the cloud name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a rain-bearing cloud, one of the standard meteorological cloud types.

clue.text: Say what you like, Britain is so different from N Korea

definitions.meaning: a shrug meaning anyone may hold or voice any opinion

definitions.text: Britain is so different from N Korea
definitions.meaning: a claim that Britain, unlike North Korea, has liberty

explanation.surface: A defence of free speech contrasting Britain with North Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning anyone may do as they wish, and literally describes a nation with liberty.

clue.text: Butterfly is absolutely filled with colour

parts.note: something that brims is full to the top
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A butterfly is completely full of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a yellow European butterfly, one of the first seen in spring.

clue.text: Pin more asymmetrical?

definitions.meaning: a pin for holding meat while cooking
a comparative of skew, meaning more lopsided; the question mark flags the invented form

explanation.surface: Is this pin bent further out of true?
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long cooking pin, and read as skew plus -er it is the comparative of skew, slanted.

clue.text: Sign off, endlessly depressed by painful condition

indicators.note: by places the first piece beside, here on top of, the second
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: someone depressed is low
gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: A doctor signs off a patient made miserable by a painful ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: To log out is to end a computer session, a modern form of signing off.

clue.text: Saw notice become out of date

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
to age is to grow old and so become dated

explanation.surface: Someone saw a notice going past its expiry date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; here it is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw in the old sense is a proverb or maxim, which is exactly what an adage is.

clue.text: In small bed, thorn tree

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a cot is a small bed, for a baby
a spine is a sharp thorn on a plant

explanation.surface: A child pricked by a thorn while in a little bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots pine is a common conifer native to northern Europe, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Give away pounds, having left nothing for artist

parts.note: to donate is to give something away
L, from the Latin libra, is the symbol for pounds sterling
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A painter gives away money and is left penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was the Florentine Renaissance sculptor, so an artist.

clue.text: Join English match

parts.note: to fuse is to join things together, as by melting

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up for a game of English sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' reads as a sporting fixture; it is the kind you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusee is a large-headed match that stays alight in wind.

clue.text: Basket-maker getting thanks for a fine biscuit

indicators.note: getting introduces the word that comes in as a replacement
for marks the swap: one letter is put in place of another

parts.note: raffia is the palm fibre woven into baskets
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A basket weaver is thanked with a nice biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ... for' puts TA in place of one F of RAFFIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratafia is a small almond-flavoured biscuit, like an amaretto.

clue.text: Up-and-coming skill, covering new roofing material in render

indicators.note: covering places the first piece on top of the rest in this down entry
in a down entry, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
slate is used for roof tiles

explanation.surface: A rising talent laying new slates on a house's render.
explanation.walkthrough: 'render' looks like the plaster on a wall; it is the verb meaning to put into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a text into another language is to put it across in a new tongue.

clue.text: A little agitation as Republican code of honour almost rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the letters are turned back to front
almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: omerta is the Mafia's code of silence and honour

explanation.surface: A political party's honour code is turned down, causing a bit of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims OMERTA to OMERT; R plus OMERT, then 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight shaking, so a small amount of agitation.

clue.text: Use scent liberally for appeal

indicators.note: applied liberally means spread freely around, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Splash on perfume generously to be more attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuteness is attractiveness, the quality of having charm or appeal.

clue.text: Chap sounds fit, for a Spaniard

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: sounds signals that the following word is heard rather than read

parts.note: fit and well both mean healthy

explanation.surface: A man seems healthy, and is suited to being Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN plus something said like WELL gives MAN-WELL, spelt the Spanish way. Manuel is the Spanish waiter in the British TV comedy Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel is a common Spanish given name, so a Spaniard might well bear it.

clue.text: Group of composers, minus nine

parts.note: less means minus, as in five less two
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A group of musicians who are short of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Six were six French composers of the 1920s, including Poulenc and Milhaud.

clue.text: French film-maker's company facing acute distress

indicators.note: to distress something is to rough it up, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A French director's firm faces a serious crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Cocteau was a French poet who directed films such as La Belle et la Bete.

clue.text: Your setter is within reach somehow for old monster

indicators.note: within means the first piece is put inside the second
somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: the setter talks of themself as I, so 'your setter is' becomes I am, shortened

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is within striking distance of an ancient beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of reach to CHERA, and 'within' puts the setter's I'M inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chimera was a fire-breathing beast of Greek myth, part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Prestige long maintained by court

indicators.note: maintained by means held within the outer piece

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A court has long upheld its standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means distinction or status, the kind of prestige a name carries.

clue.text: Parts of church show small errors, length being out

indicators.note: being out means the letter for length is removed

parts.note: lapses are small slips or mistakes

explanation.surface: Bits of a church building reveal minor faults in measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Apses are the vaulted semicircular recesses at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Make a demand, and others raise it, beginning to swagger about

indicators.note: about means the whole run of pieces before it is turned round

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others
up is what raising something does
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone demands, while others lift it, starting to strut around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole string round, including the S taken from swagger, so that S ends up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to specify a requirement, so to lay down a demand.

clue.text: One leads from heart ace, or leads from trump ace

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: leads from picks the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Bridge advice: lead a heart ace, or lead trumps from the ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' and 'heart' look like card play; the definition means a vessel leading from the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery, carrying blood out of the heart.

clue.text: High-pitched sounds each video modulated

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular register; the phrase covers the range of high notes one sings in

indicators.note: modulated means varied in pitch or tone, so the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Each video has its high notes adjusted electronically.
explanation.definitionFit: Head voice is the upper register of the singing voice, producing the higher notes.

clue.text: Wrong end of sponge cake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A baker picks the wrong end of a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge cake' looks like a single phrase; sponge only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich, often layered, central European cake.

clue.text: You need to remove middle and last line of story

parts.note: thee is the old form of you

indicators.note: to remove middle tells us the central letters of the word go

explanation.surface: An editor tells you to cut the middle and the final line of a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories traditionally close with a two-word sign-off marking their conclusion.

clue.text: Bumper corn harvest may produce this quantity of work

parts.note: a bumper crop is a big one, giving many
ears are the grain-bearing heads gathered at a corn harvest

explanation.surface: A huge grain crop might yield this much labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-year is the work one person does in a year, so the plural measures labour.
